recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not edit inactive core DeviceUsage source or add redundant filters to elements already typed only as Patient; revisit only if future generation expands clinical-patient.target beyond Patient or a new clinical-patient base has a non-Patient patient target.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-I technical correction asking that common SearchParameter patient target only Patient and that non-patient-named patient search expressions, specifically DeviceUseStatement.subject, be filtered with where(resolve() is Patient).
initial_application: The Jira comment says the work was done in R4B. No source commit was found that cites FHIR-28219 directly, but FHIR-I 2020-12-07 minutes record the decision to fix the DeviceUseStatement FHIRPath, and related R4B commit b717783b86bab2bb3aa9ca289f2cd11a7ba18107 for FHIR-26900 changed DeviceUseStatement-patient to DeviceUseStatement.subject.where(resolve() is Patient).
additional_context: DeviceUseStatement was later renamed to DeviceUsage and DeviceUsage is no longer active in the current FHIR core build; the related FHIR-26900 combined-branch audit records that the external DeviceUsage artifact preserves the Patient-only patient search semantics. Existing combined-branch audits for FHIR-31714/FHIR-32876 and the FHIR-36674 source fix cover later generated-target and registry-alignment work in the same clinical-patient change family.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. On the combined branch, SearchParameter is active, clinical-patient has no Group target assertion, patient-code SearchParameter sources have no explicit non-Patient target, Patient-only elements cover the unfiltered non-.patient expressions, and current/R5/R4B generated search-parameters.json all report clinical-patient target ["Patient"].
